title: Nay, Tell Us Not of Dangers Dire
description: Nay, Tell Us Not of Dangers Dire in Tonic Solfa to ST. FLAVIAN, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: Mirabeau B. Lamar wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 309, “The Christian Reformer”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. FLAVIAN; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Nay, tell us not of dan-gers dire That lie in du-ty's path; A war-rior of the cross can feel No fear of hu-man wrath.

lines: Nay, tell us not of dangers dire
That lie in duty's path;
A warrior of the cross can feel
No fear of human wrath.
Where'er the Prince of Darkness holds
His earthly reign abhorred,
Sword of the spirit, thee we draw,
And battle for the Lord.
We go! we go, to break the chains
That bind the erring mind,
And give the freedom that we feel
To all of human kind.
But, O, we wear no burnished steel,
And seek no gory field;
Our weapon is the word of God,
His promise is our shield.
And still serene and fixed in faith,
We fear no earthly harm;
We know it is our Father's work,
We rest upon His arm.

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: Mirabeau B. Lamar died in 1859.
credits: Words by Mirabeau B. Lamar (1798–1859), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to ST. FLAVIAN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
